newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan decapitation murder case turns more grisly.
newsitem.headline: Japan decapitation murder case turns more grisly.

text.p: A murder case involving the beheading of an 11-year-old boy turned more grisly on Thursday, as newspapers reported that mutilated animal corpses were recently found in the area of the killing.

The macabre case has drawn hundreds of journalists to this western Japanese port city, bringing more unwelcome publicity as residents' lives were returning to normal after the devastating 1995 Kobe earthquake.

"Several hundred journalists from newspapers, television and magazines have flocked to the area to cover the murder," a Kobe police spokesman said. "They are walking around and checking every single home."

The media frenzy was set off when the head of 11-year-old Jun Hase was found on Tuesday near a middle school where two young schoolgirls were attacked by a knife-wielding man in March. One 10-year-old died in that attack.
The body of the boy, who disappeared three days earlier after saying he was going to visit his grandfather's house nearby, was found near the primary school where he was a student.
Police believe the boy was strangled on Sunday night after savage cuts were made to his face.
Paper messages stuffed into the boy's mouth read "I enjoy killing people", "Stop me if you can" and "School kill".
The police spokesman said there had been no breakthrough so far in either the decapitation case or the attack on the girls.
He said police were investigating whether the incidents were linked and if the motives involved a grudge against schools.
The Asahi Evening News said that earlier this month the headless body of a pigeon was found in front of a bus stop near the site where the boy's head was found.
"Police also disclosed recent reports of mutilated animal corpses that were scattered around the city," the paper said.
"Numerous reports of mutilated cats in the area have reached police and one witness reported a group of people carrying out inhumane acts on the animals," the newspaper quoted police as saying.
Newspaper reports have also zeroed in on the appearance recently of graffiti on buildings in the murder area which resembled other paper messages stuffed into the boy's mouth.
The words "sacred", "devil" and "fight" appeared both on the paper messages and the graffiti.
Police have called in psychologists to examine the messages.
With the killer or killers still at large, all primary schools in the area have arranged to have students escorted to and from their homes with the help of teachers and parents.
Local vigilante groups, mainly elderly people, have also been formed to guard the area of mostly low-income housing estates during evening hours.
